questions.q: To which tribe, according to their clans, did the second lot come out?
questions.a: The second lot came out for Simeon, for the tribe of the sons of Simeon according to their clans.

questions.q: From which tribe’s portion was the inheritance of the sons of Simeon taken?
questions.a: The leaders of Israel had assigned more land to the tribe of Judah than it needed, so they gave part of that land to the tribe of Simeon.

questions.q: Why was the inheritance of Simeon taken from Judah’s portion?
questions.a: It was taken from Judah’s portion because the division of the sons of Judah was too great for them, so the sons of Simeon inherited in the midst of their inheritance.

questions.q: To which tribe, according to their clans, did the third lot come up?
questions.a: The third lot came up for the sons of Zebulun according to their clans.

questions.q: To which tribe, according to their clans, did the fourth lot come out?
questions.a: Joshua threw the lot again, and this time it selected the clans of the tribe of Issachar to receive the fourth part of the land.

questions.q: To which tribe, according to their clans, did the fifth lot come out?
questions.a: Joshua threw the lot again, and this time it selected the clans of the tribe of Asher to receive the fifth part of the land.

questions.q: When Joshua threw the lot again, which tribe did it select to receive the sixth part of the land?
questions.a: The sixth lot came out for the sons of Naphtali, for the sons of Naphtali according to their clans.

questions.q: How many fortified cities and their villages were included in the inheritance of the tribe of Naphtali?
questions.a: The inheritance of the tribe of Naphtali included 19 cities and their villages.

questions.q: To which tribe, according to their clans, did the seventh lot come out?
questions.a: The seventh lot came out for the tribe of the sons of Dan according to their clans.

questions.q: What city did the sons of Israel give to Joshua son of Nun as an inheritance in their midst, upon Yahweh’s command?
questions.a: Upon the mouth of Yahweh, they gave him the city that he requested, Timnath Serah in the hill country of Ephraim.

commentary.text: The lot of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and Dan.

Verses 1–9 The men of Judah did not oppose taking away the cities within their border, when convinced that they had more than was right. If a true believer has obtained an unintended and improper advantage in any thing, he will give it up without murmuring. Love seeketh not her own, and doth not behave unseemly; it will induce those in whom it richly dwells, to part with their own to supply what is lacking to their brethren.

In the division to each tribe of Israel, the prophetic blessings of Jacob were fulfilled. They chose for themselves, or it was divided to them by lot, in the manner and places that he foresaw. So sure a rule to go by is the word of prophecy: we see by it what to believe, and it proves beyond all dispute the things that are of God.

Joshua waited till all the tribes were settled, before he asked any provision for himself. He was content to be unfixed, till he saw them all placed, and herein is an example to all in public places, to prefer the common welfare before private advantage. Those who labour most to do good to others, seek an inheritance in the Canaan above: but it will be soon enough to enter thereon, when they have done all the service to their brethren of which they are capable. Nor can any thing more effectually assure them of their title to it, than endeavouring to bring others to desire, to seek, and to obtain it. Our Lord Jesus came and dwelt on earth, not in pomp but poverty, providing rest for man, yet himself not having where to lay his head; for Christ pleased not himself. Nor would he enter upon his inheritance, till by his obedience to death he secured the eternal inheritance for all his people; nor will he account his own glory completed, till every ransomed sinner is put in possession of his heavenly rest.
